items.stated_text: This rapid adoption of AI tools, however, stands in contrast to the current legal landscape of North Macedonia, which currently lacks a specific regulatory framework to govern the development, deployment, or use of AI.
items.summary: North Macedonia currently lacks a specific regulatory framework for developing, deploying or using AI, in contrast to rapid adoption of AI tools.

items.stated_text: Without this alignment, the country risks regulatory fragmentation, decreased trust in AI systems, and potential delays in the accession process. Failure to harmonise national legislation with the acquis communautaire—specifically the AI Act in this case—would signal insufficient compliance with EU digital and data protection standards, undermine the country’s credibility as an EU candidate and weaken its still-developing data protection framework.
items.summary: Without AI Act alignment the country risks fragmentation, lower trust and accession delays; failure would undermine its credibility and its data protection framework.

items.summary: North Macedonia can use the AI Act's application milestones of 2025, 2026 and 2027 to guide gradual alignment of its frameworks.

This inadequacy is particularly in relation to critical issues such as algorithmic bias, accountability for automated decision-making processes, and the broad application of AI across diverse economic and social sectors.

items.stated_text: Its broad definition of “processing of personal data” in Article 4, paragraph (1), point 2, encompassing automated means, allows the Personal Data Protection Agency (the Agency) to oversee AI systems handling personal data. Similarly, Article 4, paragraph (1), point 4’s definition of “profiling” directly applies to many AI applications, establishing a legal basis for regulating predictive AI.
items.summary: The law's definitions of processing and profiling allow the Agency to oversee AI systems handling personal data and regulate predictive AI.

location.section: North Macedonia’s Current Regulatory Landscape for AI

items.stated_text: Furthermore, data subjects’ rights in Article 17, paragraph (2), point 6, and Article 18, paragraph (2), point 7, specifically address “automated decision-making process, including profiling,” granting individuals the right to meaningful information about AI logic and consequences. This empowers them to understand and challenge algorithmic decisions.
items.summary: The law gives individuals a right to meaningful information on automated decision-making, including profiling, so they can understand and challenge algorithmic decisions.

location.section: North Macedonia’s Current Regulatory Landscape for AI

items.stated_text: Finally, the Agency’s broad powers under Article 66 to demand information and access personal data provide a crucial regulatory mecha - nism to investigate and enforce data protection compliance in AI-related cases.
items.summary: The Agency's powers to demand information and access personal data provide a mechanism to enforce data protection in AI-related cases.

items.stated_text: North Macedonia currently lacks a dedicated legal framework for artificial intelligence. While broader digital transformation efforts are underway—most notably through the National ICT Strategy—the country still does not regulate AI-specific risks, responsibilities, or oversight mechanisms.
items.summary: North Macedonia lacks a dedicated AI legal framework and does not regulate AI-specific risks, responsibilities or oversight, despite broader digital transformation efforts.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment

items.stated_text: The absence of legally defined safeguards, institutional capacity, and technical infrastructure creates a gap between North Macedonia’s current position and the standards required by the EU AI Act.
items.summary: Missing legal safeguards, institutional capacity and technical infrastructure create a gap between the country's position and EU AI Act standards.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment

items.stated_text: The absence of a dedicated national AI strategy means North Macedonia must start from scratch, requiring substantial political will, financial investment, and legal expertise to build a comprehensive regulatory framework. Securing ade - quate funding for these reforms will be a significant challenge, likely necessitating international support.
items.summary: With no national AI strategy, the country must start from scratch, needing political will, money and expertise; funding will likely need international support.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Legal Changes

items.stated_text: Given the complexity and breadth of the EU AI Act, North Macedonia should adopt a new, dedicated law on artificial intelligence rather than attempting to regulate AI solely through amendments to the existing Law on Personal Data Protection.
items.summary: North Macedonia should adopt a new dedicated AI law rather than regulating AI only through amendments to the data protection law.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Legal Changes

items.stated_text: While the LPDP addresses issues related to data governance and individual rights, it does not cover criti - cal aspects such as risk classification, conformity assessments, or sector-specific obligations.
items.summary: The data protection law covers data governance and individual rights but not risk classification, conformity assessments or sector-specific obligations.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Legal Changes

items.stated_text: This law should adopt a risk-based classification, mir - roring the EU AI Act, and explicitly prohibit systems deemed to pose an unacceptable risk.
items.summary: The new law should adopt risk-based classification mirroring the AI Act and explicitly prohibit systems posing unacceptable risk.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Legal Changes

items.stated_text: This legislation must also mandate fundamental rights impact assessments for high-risk AI systems before their deployment, providing a means to proactively address these harms and risks.
items.summary: The legislation must mandate fundamental rights impact assessments for high-risk AI systems before they are deployed.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Legal Changes

items.stated_text: For systems classified as high-risk, North Macedonia will need to legislate requirements covering data governance (similar to those found in the LPDP), comprehensive tech - nical documentation and record-keeping, and transparency and information provisions.
items.summary: North Macedonia will need to legislate data governance, technical documentation, record-keeping and transparency requirements for high-risk AI systems.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Legal Changes

items.stated_text: This can include specifying requirements for post-market monitoring and reporting of serious incidents involving AI systems, ensuring ongoing compliance and accountability once systems become operational, that is, deployed and accessible to many users.
items.summary: The law can include post-market monitoring and reporting of serious incidents involving AI systems.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Legal Changes

items.stated_text: It must ensure meaningful human oversight, guarantee the technical robustness, accuracy, and cybersecurity of highrisk AI systems, and mandate the establishment of a robust risk management system.
items.summary: The law must ensure human oversight, technical robustness, accuracy and cybersecurity of high-risk AI systems, and mandate a risk management system.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Legal Changes

items.stated_text: The new law must also establish transparency obligations for limited-risk AI systems, such as chatbots, and define a clear enforcement framework with designated national authorities and a system of penalties consistent with the EU Act, including provisions for redress mechanisms for affected individuals.
items.summary: The law must set transparency obligations for limited-risk AI, and an enforcement framework with national authorities, penalties and redress for affected individuals.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Legal Changes

items.stated_text: Beyond a general AI law, existing sector-specific legislation in areas such as healthcare, finance, employment, and education will need to be reviewed and amended to incorporate AI-specific provisions, ensuring consistency with the principles of the AI Act.
items.summary: Sector legislation on healthcare, finance, employment and education needs review and amendment to incorporate AI-specific provisions consistent with the AI Act.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Legal Changes

items.stated_text: North Macedonia will need to designate a competent national authority for AI oversight, potentially expanding its Personal Data Protection Agency (PDPA) or creating a dedicated AI body with multidisciplinary experts.
items.summary: North Macedonia must designate a competent AI oversight authority, possibly by expanding the data protection agency or creating a dedicated body.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Institutional Changes

items.stated_text: For high-risk AI systems or developers, inde - pendent third-party conformity assessment bodies must be accredited or established.
items.summary: Independent third-party conformity assessment bodies must be accredited or established for high-risk AI systems or developers.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Institutional Changes

items.stated_text: However, the PDPA itself faces well-documented limitations. Its annual reports and the European Commission’s most recent progress report identify persistent challenges such as limited staffing, insufficient funding, and a lack of technical infrastructure, which severely constrain its regulatory reach.
items.summary: The data protection agency's limited staffing, funding and technical infrastructure severely constrain its regulatory reach.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Institutional Changes

items.stated_text: Extensive training is necessary for civil servants across all government sectors, including ministries, the judiciary, and procurement, to develop their understanding of both the legal requirements and technical implications of the AI Act.
items.summary: Civil servants across government, including ministries, the judiciary and procurement, need extensive training on the legal and technical implications of the AI Act.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Institutional Changes

items.stated_text: In addition, the designated AI authority, whether new or existing, must be significantly equipped with human, financial, and technological resources to carry out its mission effectively.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Institutional Changes

items.stated_text: Building institutional capacity will demand coordinated efforts to train public officials and establish competent au - thorities to oversee AI deployment and compliance.
items.summary: Building capacity will demand coordinated efforts to train public officials and establish competent authorities to oversee AI deployment and compliance.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Institutional Changes

items.stated_text: Developing or adopting detailed technical standards for AI development and deployment, consistent with European norms (including both explainable AI and interoperability), is vital.
items.summary: Developing or adopting AI technical standards consistent with European norms, including explainable AI and interoperability, is vital.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Technical Changes

items.stated_text: Investment is needed to develop a national pool of AI experts, including ethics specialists, data scientists, and engineers, within both public and private sectors, as well as to bolster educational programs and AI research.

location.section: Necessary Legal, Institutional, and Technical Changes for Alignment > Technical Changes

items.stated_text: Establishing or supporting AI testing and validation facilities, especially for high-risk system testing, is essential for compliance.

items.summary: North Macedonia must develop incentives, career programmes and research funding to retain digital and AI professionals and prevent brain drain.
